source_row.rationale: In advanced CKD, impaired phosphate excretion and reduced calcitriol activity contribute to phosphate retention and lower serum calcium, often with secondary hyperparathyroidism. Hypocalcemia is therefore the best answer. Hypercalcemia is the opposite calcium pattern, while hypernatremia and hypermagnesemia are not the characteristic paired abnormality tested in CKD mineral-bone disorder.
source_row.source_detail: StatPearls Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral Bone Disorder — Pathophysiology: declining kidney function impairs phosphate excretion and calcitriol production, contributing to hyperphosphatemia, lower serum calcium or hypocalcemia, and secondary hyperparathyroidism in advanced CKD.
